info.doc: heaven bench NAME|URL [-n 100] [-c 10] [--max-p95 MS]
heaven compare NAME --env A --env B heaven compare get /path --env A --env B
heaven env set|use|list|show|rm
Send a template, show the result, and decide the exit code. Used by: <method>, run, replay.
heaven flow FILE.json
heaven history [show ID | clear] · heaven replay ID
Every command, in one place. router.js maps command words to these functions.
heaven init — create a project-local .heaven/ folder (meant to be committed, minus history).
heaven get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options URL [options]
Saved requests: save · list · run · rm

Helpers used by several commands. Every command receives a `ctx` object (built in cli.js): ctx.pos positional words ctx.flags parsed flags ctx.out stdout (data) ctx.err stderr (messages) ctx.c colours for stderr ctx.cout
Everything printed after a request: verbose headers, body, status line, check results.

The single list of every flag Heaven understands. To add a new flag: add one line here, then read it from `flags` in a command. Flags that take a value. name -> { short?, list? } `list: true` means the flag may repeat (-
All help text. GENERAL -> `heaven help` COMMANDS[name] -> `heaven help <name>` Conventions used throughout: UPPERCASE placeholder you replace [brackets] optional a | b choose one ... may be repeated
Small helpers that turn raw flag strings into structured values.
Load generator: fire `count` requests with at most `concurrency` in flight. Response bodies are read and discarded (never buffered).
Small statistics helpers for benchmark results.
Field-by-field JSON diff with ignore patterns.
Pull a value out of a response for use in later steps. status · headers.location · body.a.b[0] · body

Run a workflow: ordered steps that extract values from responses and feed them into later steps as {{variables}}. Stops at the first failing step unless continueOnError is set (on the step or on the whole flow).
Convert one workflow step (as written in the JSON file) into a request template.
Turn a template body into the resolved body the HTTP engine sends, and set sensible default Content-Type headers.
Case-insensitive header helpers (HTTP header names are case-insensitive).
Template + environment + variables -> fully-resolved, ready-to-send request. Pipeline: variables → base URL → env default headers → query → auth → body.
The one code path every command uses to send something: template → (env + vars) → resolved request → HTTP → history.

A request *template* is the saved/editable form of a request: { method, url, headers, query[], body, auth, timeout, follow, expect } It keeps {{placeholders}} unresolved so it can be saved, replayed, and sent to any envi
URL handling: base-URL joining and query-string building.
Decide whether a buffered body is binary, text, or JSON.
Sends one fully-resolved request and returns a normalized response object.
Translate low-level fetch/Node errors into friendly HeavenError / NetworkError messages.

Three ways to consume a response body, chosen by the caller. All are memory-safe: outputFile -> stream straight to disk (never buffered) onChunk -> hand chunks to the caller as they arrive (SSE, NDJSON, big streams) disc
Turn our internal body description into something `fetch` accepts.
History is a JSON-lines file (one entry per line, newest last).
Read/write one JSON file safely.
Decide which directory holds Heaven's data.
The Store is the one object commands use to touch disk. It owns three files: config.json (environments), requests.json (saved requests), history.jsonl
Run an expectation against a response. Each kind of check is its own small function that returns { ok, label, detail? }, so adding a new check is easy.
Turn --expect-* flags (and flow "expect" blocks) into a normalized expectation object.
ANSI colours, automatically disabled when output isn't a terminal or NO_COLOR is set.
Number/time formatting helpers.
One import for everything presentation-related.
Syntax-highlight pretty-printed JSON for terminals.
Formatting for a single HTTP response.
Plain-text table with aligned columns (ANSI-colour aware).
Questions we ask about a template: "does it hold secrets?" and "where were they redacted?"
What counts as "sensitive". Shared by redaction and the save/env warnings.

Produce a safe-to-persist copy of a request template (used for history). A *literal secret* is a sensitive-looking value that is NOT a {{placeholder}}. Placeholders are safe to store because the real value lives elsewher
Shared error types and exit codes. Exit codes are part of Heaven's public contract: scripts and CI can tell *why* a command failed without parsing text.
A tiny path language used by --expect-json, flow `extract`, and compare --ignore. a.b[0].c ["odd key"] leading "$." or "$" is optional
Program entry: parse arguments, build the shared context, run the command, map errors to exit codes.
Decide which command a user typed. Commands live in ./commands/.

stats.description: Designed for speed, extensibility, and a clean developer experience, Heaven brings API development, testing, workflow automation, and performance analysis together in one powerful tool.
